PMID 33980574, abstract only (no PMC). Quote verbatim in abstract; same paper puts mouse, NHP and human systemic-tau rise side by side, so same is supported. NCT02820896 has no posted results (checked CT.gov API).

But same->same breaks one-entry-per-change; drop as separate entry, fold TANGO figures into the 2021 judgement. comparison_stated=true is marginal: paper cites mouse ISF removal in intro/discussion, no quantitative side-by-side.

missing: No missing cells. Semorinemab Lauriet (moderate AD, NCT03828747; Monteiro 2023, Neurology) showed a partial ADAS-Cog11 effect that Shulman 2023 cites; it is a different population (moderate AD) so belongs to a sibling context, not this one.
Tilavonemab early-AD phase 2 (Florian 2023, Brain, NCT02880956) is already carried in the efficacy judgement; no extra entry needed since the status is unchanged.

Context note says all four failed 'despite real engagement of N-terminal tau': for zagotenemab only plasma p-tau181/total tau rose dose-dependently and Fleisher 2024 states 'There was no direct biomarker evidence of central tau target engagement' (verbatim). Soften the note to 'peripheral/CSF engagement' or 'three of four'.
rule_questions: Engagement `same` on one unproven class member: Fleisher 2024 reports absence of a central-engagement biomarker for zagotenemab, not a contradicted prediction, and gosuranemab/semorinemab matched the mouse read-outs (ISF/plasma tau), so under the brief (>=1 drug matched; contra needs a wrong prediction) the cell stays `same`. But the species the mice modelled (seeding-competent, MTBR-containing aggregates) was never shown engaged in any patient; the brief has no status for 'matched on a proxy read-out, hypothesised species untested'.

One entry per change of status: when a later patients-only, registry-backed source (Shulman 2023) confirms a status first published from an abstract-only phase 1 paper (Ayalon 2021), the rule keeps the weaker citation as the entry and demotes the stronger one to `judgement`. Decided here: first-publication entry stands (2021 engagement, 2022 efficacy), 2023 Shulman folded into their judgements.

Dose cell opens in 2022 at the publication of the statement because the exposure model is unpublished; rule 6 (open the strip at first model use) cannot be applied to an unpublished model, so the strip shows no 'existed before tested' gap for dose.

Efficacy `contra` where the source's own explanation is epitope/isoform mismatch (the model reported its own biology correctly but was the wrong model for the question) still counts as a wrong prediction under the brief; decided contra.
